spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶1:** [GAP-1] Divine wisdom — behold, in the first state, falsity from evil was powerful against it; [GAP-2] no internal division [GAP-3] exists within wisdom itself.

*That is: the assault of falsity upon divine truth was great in the beginning, yet wisdom possesses an inherent unity that falsity cannot reproduce. All genuine truths cohere in one; no truth contradicts another, for they proceed from a single Divine origin.*

**¶2:** [GAP-4] how far [GAP-5] the divine truth that proceeded from [GAP-6] in that state in a [GAP-7] sole [GAP-8] the fullness of divine wisdom was in mutual accord forever, and not one truth transgressed the order and law that its companion truth had committed to it eternally.

*That is: all truths that proceed from the Divine exist in perfect mutual harmony. Each truth holds its place within the universal order. None departs from the arrangement ordained among them, because they share a single origin in the Divine Good and therefore cannot contradict one another. This is the nature of heavenly order — each particular truth serves and sustains every other.*

**¶3:** However, falsity from evil, the adversary of all truth, was destined to perish and to be overcome; because of the arising of internal contradiction it was divided against itself. Even its dominion was divided against itself; [GAP-9] ev[en] the [GAP-10] derivative falsities and evil affections, which had ascended out of their infernal depths and risen up in pursuit of dominion, were destined to perish because of the self-contradiction that was present throughout all of them. Falsity from evil was destroyed, and its subordinate powers of persuasion were brought to nothing.

*That is: evil and falsity bear within themselves the cause of their own dissolution. Because evil loves only itself, every particular evil contests with every other; falsity contradicts falsity. A dominion built on self-love cannot cohere, for each part seeks supremacy over every other. The derivative falsities that rise up out of the deepest hells carry this same contradiction within them. Therefore evil is not overcome from without alone, but collapses from within — its very nature is disintegration, whereas the nature of divine truth is unity. This is the spiritual law by which the hells are ultimately subdued: what is divided against itself cannot stand, while what is one in the Divine stands forever.*

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: [Now as to what affects the] Light, behold, at the beginning the Darkness was strong against it; [yet] no disunity [or discord] exists in the Light.

[See] how far [extends the Lig]ht that came forth from [the Greatness] in that place in a [will] alone [they shared] the greatness of the Light with one another for ever, and nor did one of them transgress the command and order that his brother had entrusted to him forever.

However, the Darkness, the enemy, was doomed and overcome; because of the arising of disharmony it was divided within itself. Even the kingdom was divided within itself; [and] ev[en] the [powers, who had] left their abyss behind and come up fo[llow-ing] it, were doomed because of the disunity that was present in all of them. The Darkness was destroyed, and its other powers were humiliated,

fills.explanation: This is a standard Kephalaia chapter-opening formula introducing a new topic; it fits the spiritual reading's introductory function before "Light/Divine wisdom" and matches the register of the text.

The spiritual reading frames this as a contrast ("the assault was great, yet wisdom possesses an inherent unity"), requiring a contrastive conjunction between the Darkness's strength and the Light's inherent unity.

Kephalaia style regularly employs doublets for negative qualities; "no disunity or discord" pairs the static condition (disunity) with its active manifestation (discord), matching the spiritual sense of complete internal coherence in wisdom.

The Kephalaia commonly opens expository paragraphs with the imperative "See" (Coptic ⲁⲛⲁⲩ) to direct attention, and the spiritual reading indicates this is an invitation to behold how far divine truth extends.

The construction "how far extends the Light" uses inverted Coptic syntax to express the extent/reach of divine truth proceeding from its source, fitting the spiritual reading's emphasis on truth's expansive mutual harmony.

In Manichaean Kephalaia, the Father of Greatness is the supreme source of Light; "the Greatness" is the standard short form for this divine origin from which all Light proceeds, corresponding to the Divine from which truth emanates.

The Light elements exist "in a will alone" — a single divine will — which explains why none transgressed the command entrusted by his brother; this corresponds to all truths sharing one origin in Divine Good and therefore acting in perfect accord.

The spiritual reading states "the fullness of divine wisdom was in mutual accord forever"; "they shared the greatness of the Light with one another" captures this reciprocal harmony among all truths proceeding from one source.

The editor's "and" correctly links the parallel "even...even..." clauses describing the progressive self-destruction of the Darkness's kingdom, matching the spiritual reading's escalating catalogue of internal contradictions.

The editor's "powers, who had" correctly identifies these as the derivative dark forces (powers/ⲉⲝⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ) who ascended from the abyss; this corresponds to the spiritual reading's "derivative falsities and evil affections, which had ascended out of their infernal depths."
